_why: build-doc §11 stress fixture — `fixtures/mega-node.json` (all lines, counts ×100) — and §12 perf budget: ecosim.step must stay inside balance.perf.ecosimStepBudgetMs × balance.perf.megaNodeMarginMultiplier on it. Synthetic, and DELIBERATELY NOT A LEGAL NODE: every non-starter line of species.json sits in one node at ×100, which no biome admits. That is the point of it now, and it is stated rather than assumed. (1) It stresses the per-line loop of ecosim.step at 24 lines. (2) It is the only node in the repo that can BIND bible §5's "in its habitat" clause: core/schemas.ts rejects any shipped node holding a line its biome excludes, so on shipped data the habitat filter in deriveFoodWeb is unreachable and deleting it left the whole suite green. tests/property/foodweb.test.ts::"the habitat clause is LOAD-BEARING" uses this fixture and fails if the filter goes. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, measured rather than claimed: the O(n²) web derivation here runs over the 7 lines the Forest biome admits, not 24 — no single node on shipped content can host more, because bible §4's habitat column splits 27 lines across six biomes. build-doc §13's "O(n²) web derivation fine at 27 lines" is measured directly instead, by tests/property/ecosim.test.ts::"measures the O(n²) derivation at the width build-doc §13 actually claims", which widens every habitat and steps the full roster. See docs/DEVIATIONS-lane-a2.md A2-D9. The three bible §4 starters are left out (habitat "starter" — handed out by Warden Maren, never encountered), and the three Ancients keep count 1 because an Ancient is a single individual. breedRate is the shipped rate for that line's role; carryCap ×3 as in data/nodes/*.json.
name: Mega Node
